newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY PARLIAMENT SETS UP JEWISH COMPENSATION BODY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY PARLIAMENT SETS UP JEWISH COMPENSATION BODY.

text.p: The Hungarian parliament voted on Wednesday to create a foundation to compensate Hungary's Jewish Holocaust survivors, the national news agency said.

The parliament's approval caps an effort of several years duration by the Jewish community in Hungary and abroad to have the Hungarian government provide compensation to survivors of the Nazi campaign to exterminate the Jews.

The motion sets up a public foundation with assets including real estate, antiques, cash and compensation coupons worth almost seven billion forints ($45 million) at official value) and cash, MTI reported.
Compensation coupons may be exchanged for life annuity policies. Payments from the public foundation will only be available to Jews living in Hungary.
The board of the public foundation will comprise representatives of the Jewish community, the government and leading public figures.
The Association of Jewish Religious Communities in Hungary (MAZSIHISZ) and the international World Jewish Restitution Organisation will contribute to the public foundation.
The largest opposition party, the Independent Smallholders, voted against the motion while other opposition MPs abstained.

There are an estimated 20,000 Hungarian Jewish survivors of the Holocaust in Hungary. Before World War Two the country had an estimated 800,000 to one million Jews, one of the wealthiest Jewish communities in Europe.
The Hungarian government agreed to establish the public foundation in July after talks with the World Jewish Congress and other groups, but the act needed parliamentary approval.
